page: Amazon Web Services gr6.8xlarge is a graphics-intensive server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is equipped with an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.4 GHz, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores. The system features 256 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Graphics and compute acceleration are handled by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing 22 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 900 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is rated at a baseline of 25 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core and Passmark CPU encryption tests scoring in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and general database operations fall within the average tier. However, the hardware demonstrates top-tier performance in machine learning workloads, placing in the top 10% for LLM inference speeds during prompt processing and text generation with small and medium models. Prompt processing for large 70B models also registers strong performance in the top 25%.

From a resource-density perspective, the gr6.8xlarge provides a balanced profile by combining dedicated AMD EPYC processing, high-capacity DDR4 memory, and a modern Ada Lovelace GPU on a single instance. This configuration is highly suited for graphics-intensive applications, medium-scale LLM inference, machine learning development, and database operations requiring fast local NVMe SSD storage.
